base.name: RV32I
base.desc: Core 32-bit integer instruction set of loads, stores, arithmetic and branches that every RV32 core implements.
base.use: Deeply embedded cores with a 32-bit address space

base.name: RV64I
base.desc: The 64-bit integer base, widening registers and addresses to 64 bits for large-memory application-class systems.

base.name: RV32E
base.desc: Halves the integer register file to 16 registers, cutting area and power in the smallest embedded cores.

base.name: RV64E
base.desc: Embedded 64-bit base with only 16 integer registers, trading register count for smaller, cheaper cores.

base.name: RV128I
base.desc: Widens the integer registers and the address space to 128 bits for machines that outgrow 64-bit addressing.
base.use: Address spaces beyond 64 bits; encoding not final

standard.name: A
standard.desc: Atomic read-modify-write and load-reserved/store-conditional instructions for synchronizing harts sharing memory.

standard.name: B
standard.desc: Umbrella for the Zba, Zbb and Zbs bit-manipulation extensions, signaled to software by a single misa bit.

standard.name: C
standard.desc: Short 16-bit encodings of common instructions, typically cutting program size by 25 to 30 percent.

standard.name: D
standard.desc: Double-precision IEEE 754 arithmetic on 64-bit floating-point registers, building on the F extension.

standard.name: F
standard.desc: Single-precision IEEE 754 arithmetic with 32 floating-point registers and a status register for rounding modes.

standard.name: H
standard.desc: A second stage of address translation and a guest privilege mode so hypervisors can host guest operating systems.

henvcfgh.desc: most-significant 32 bits of Hypervisor Environment Configuration

hgatp.desc: Hypervisor guest address translation and protection

hstateen0h.desc: Upper 32 bits of Hypervisor State Enable 0 Register

hstateen1h.desc: Upper 32 bits of Hypervisor State Enable 1 Register

hstateen2h.desc: Upper 32 bits of Hypervisor State Enable 2 Register

hstateen3h.desc: Upper 32 bits of Hypervisor State Enable 3 Register

vsatp.desc: Virtual Supervisor Address Translation and Protection

standard.name: M
standard.desc: Integer multiply and divide instructions, kept out of the base so minimal cores can leave them out.

standard.name: N
standard.desc: Delivers traps directly to user mode so a handler can run without entering supervisor or machine mode.

standard.name: P
standard.desc: Packed fixed-point SIMD arithmetic in the integer registers, aimed at DSP kernels on cores with no vector unit.

standard.name: Q
standard.desc: Quad-precision IEEE 754 arithmetic on 128-bit floating-point registers, for math needing more range than double.

standard.name: S
standard.desc: Supervisor privilege level with its own CSRs and address translation, the level an operating system kernel runs in.

standard.name: U
standard.desc: Least privileged execution level, where application code runs isolated from the kernel and the platform.

standard.name: V
standard.desc: Variable-length vector registers and data-parallel operations that scale across implementations without recompiling.

standard.name: Sm
standard.desc: Machine privilege level, the highest one, entered at reset and used for low-level control of the hardware platform.
standard.use: Firmware and boot code at the highest privilege

henvcfgh.desc: most-significant 32 bits of Hypervisor Environment Configuration

z_bit.name: Zba
z_bit.desc: Shift-and-add instructions that compute an array element address in one operation instead of several.

z_bit.name: Zbb
z_bit.desc: Common bit and word operations such as count leading zeros, population count, min/max, rotate and sign extend.
z_bit.use: Bit counting, min/max and byte swapping

z_bit.name: Zbc
z_bit.desc: Carry-less multiplication over GF(2) polynomials, the primitive behind CRC and Galois-field cryptography.

z_bit.name: Zbs
z_bit.desc: Set, clear, invert or test a single bit at a computed index without a mask-and-shift sequence.

z_atomics.name: Za128rs
z_atomics.desc: Guarantees the LR/SC reservation set is contiguous, naturally aligned and no larger than 128 bytes.

z_atomics.name: Za64rs
z_atomics.desc: Guarantees the LR/SC reservation set is contiguous, naturally aligned and no larger than 64 bytes.

z_atomics.name: Zaamo
z_atomics.desc: Atomic read-modify-write operations on memory such as swap, add, logical, min and max, with no LR/SC pair.

z_atomics.name: Zabha
z_atomics.desc: Byte and halfword widths for the atomic memory operations, useful for subword locks, flags and counters.

z_atomics.name: Zacas
z_atomics.desc: Compare-and-swap on words, doublewords and quadwords, the primitive that lock-free data structures need.

z_atomics.name: Zalasr
z_atomics.desc: Load-acquire and store-release memory instructions, giving ordered accesses without full fences.

z_atomics.name: Zalrsc
z_atomics.desc: Load-reserved and store-conditional pairs used to build read-modify-write atomic sequences.

z_atomics.name: Zama16b
z_atomics.desc: Misaligned loads, stores, and AMOs that stay within an aligned 16-byte block execute atomically.

z_atomics.name: Zawrs
z_atomics.desc: Lets a hart idle in a low-power state while polling a memory location for another agent's update.

z_atomics.name: Ziccrse
z_atomics.desc: Main memory must eventually let a load-reserved/store-conditional loop succeed, so locks make progress.

z_compress.name: Zca
z_compress.desc: The C extension's 16-bit encodings minus the floating-point loads and stores, for cores without an FPU.

z_compress.name: Zcb
z_compress.desc: Short 16-bit encodings for common byte, halfword, sign-extend, and multiply operations to shrink code.

z_compress.name: Zcd
z_compress.desc: Shrinks double-precision code by encoding its floating-point loads and stores in 16 bits.

z_compress.name: Zce
z_compress.desc: Bundles the code-size-reduction Zc extensions that microcontroller-class cores are expected to implement.

z_compress.name: Zcf
z_compress.desc: Shrinks single-precision code on RV32 by encoding its floating-point loads and stores in 16 bits.

z_compress.name: Zcmp
z_compress.desc: Single instructions that push or pop a list of saved registers, collapsing prologues and epilogues.

z_compress.name: Zcmt
z_compress.desc: Calls functions through an index into a jump table, replacing call sequences with two-byte instructions.

jvt.desc: Table Jump Base Vector and Control Register

z_compress.name: Zcmop
z_compress.desc: Reserves eight 16-bit no-op encodings that future extensions can redefine without breaking older code.

z_compress.name: Zclsd
z_compress.desc: Loads or stores a register pair in a single 16-bit RV32 instruction, cutting code size further.

z_float.name: Zdinx
z_float.desc: Double-precision arithmetic carried out in integer register pairs, so no separate FP register file is needed.
z_float.use: Double precision with no separate FP register file

z_float.name: Zfa
z_float.desc: Immediate loads, IEEE 754-2019 min/max, round-to-integer, and quiet comparisons missing from base FP.
z_float.use: IEEE operations missing from base F and D

z_float.name: Zfbfmin
z_float.desc: Converts between BFloat16 and 32-bit floats, making BF16 usable as a compact interchange format.

z_float.name: Zfh
z_float.desc: IEEE 754-2008 16-bit arithmetic, for workloads where reduced precision saves memory and power.

z_float.name: Zfhmin
z_float.desc: Half-precision load, store, and conversion only, for code that stores in 16 bits but computes wider.

z_float.name: Zfinx
z_float.desc: Single-precision arithmetic carried out in the integer registers, cutting the cost of small cores.
z_float.use: Single precision with no separate FP register file

z_float.name: Zhinx
z_float.desc: Half-precision arithmetic carried out in the integer registers instead of a separate FP register file.
z_float.use: Half precision with no separate FP register file

z_float.name: Zhinxmin
z_float.desc: Half-precision conversion instructions only, operating on the integer registers rather than FP ones.

z_load_store.name: Zicclsm
z_load_store.desc: Requires misaligned loads and stores to work in cacheable coherent main memory, though possibly slowly.
z_load_store.use: Software that assumes misaligned access works

z_load_store.name: Zilsd
z_load_store.desc: Loads or stores an even-odd register pair in one RV32 instruction instead of two separate accesses.

z_integer.name: Zicond
z_integer.desc: Conditional zeroing operations that let compilers build branchless selects in two-instruction sequences.

z_integer.name: Zmmul
z_integer.desc: Integer multiply without divide, for low-cost cores where divider hardware is not worth the area.

z_vector.name: Zve32x
z_vector.desc: Integer, fixed-point, mask, and permute vector operations on elements up to 32 bits, with no floating-point needed.

z_vector.name: Zve32f
z_vector.desc: Single-precision vector floating-point on top of the Zve32x embedded subset, with elements still capped at 32 bits.

z_vector.name: Zve64x
z_vector.desc: Integer and fixed-point vector operations on elements up to 64 bits, for embedded cores that need no floating-point.

z_vector.name: Zve64f
z_vector.desc: Single-precision vector floating-point alongside 64-bit integer elements, for embedded cores that skip FP64.

z_vector.name: Zve64d
z_vector.desc: Double-precision vector floating-point on top of Zve64f, completing embedded FP support at 64-bit element width.

z_vector.name: Zvl32b
z_vector.desc: Guarantees a vector register length of at least 32 bits, so LMUL=1 holds only four byte-sized elements.
z_vector.use: Code that requires VLEN of at least 32 bits

z_vector.name: Zvl64b
z_vector.desc: Guarantees a vector register length of at least 64 bits, so LMUL=1 holds eight byte-sized elements.
z_vector.use: Code that requires VLEN of at least 64 bits

z_vector.name: Zvl128b
z_vector.desc: Guarantees a vector register length of at least 128 bits, the minimum the full V extension requires.
z_vector.use: Code that requires VLEN of at least 128 bits

z_vector.name: Zvl256b
z_vector.desc: Guarantees a vector register length of at least 256 bits, so LMUL=1 holds 32 byte-sized elements.
z_vector.use: Code that requires VLEN of at least 256 bits

z_vector.name: Zvl512b
z_vector.desc: Guarantees a vector register length of at least 512 bits, so LMUL=1 holds 64 byte-sized elements.
z_vector.use: Code that requires VLEN of at least 512 bits

z_vector.name: Zvl1024b
z_vector.desc: Guarantees a vector register length of at least 1024 bits, so LMUL=1 holds 128 byte-sized elements.
z_vector.use: Code that requires VLEN of at least 1024 bits

z_vector.name: Zvfh
z_vector.desc: Full IEEE binary16 arithmetic on vector elements, including compares, reductions, and 8-bit integer conversions.

z_vector.name: Zvfhmin
z_vector.desc: Converts vector elements between binary16 and binary32 only, for cheap half-precision storage without FP16 math.

z_vector.name: Zvfbfmin
z_vector.desc: Converts vector elements between BF16 and FP32, just enough to use BF16 as a compact interchange format.

z_vector.name: Zvfbfa
z_vector.desc: Extends vector floating-point arithmetic to work on BF16 elements directly, beyond conversion and widening multiply-add.

z_vector.name: Zvfbfwma
z_vector.desc: Widening multiply-add over BF16 vector elements accumulating into FP32, the inner loop of BF16 matrix math.

z_vector.name: Zvfofp8min
z_vector.desc: Basic vector conversions for the 8-bit OFP8 E4M3 and E5M2 float formats used in low-precision machine learning.

z_vector.name: Zvabd
z_vector.desc: Element-wise absolute difference on integer vectors, with widening accumulate forms for video and imaging.

z_vector.name: Zvbb
z_vector.desc: Bit-level operations on vector elements such as and-not, bit and byte reversal, zero counts, and rotations.

z_vector.name: Zvbc
z_vector.desc: Carryless multiply on 64-bit vector elements, the primitive behind GHASH, elliptic-curve math, and CRC.

z_vector.name: Zvbdota
z_vector.desc: Batched dot products of one vector against eight others, accumulating eight results for tiled matrix multiply.

z_vector.name: Zvdota
z_vector.desc: Reduces two vector register groups to one accumulated dot-product scalar, over integer, BF16, or FP8 data.

z_vector.name: Zvdot4a
z_vector.desc: Four-way dot product of the packed 8-bit integers inside each 32-bit vector element, accumulated in place.

z_security.name: Smcfiss
z_security.desc: Enables Zicfiss shadow stacks in machine mode through mseccfg.MSSE, protecting firmware return addresses.

z_security.name: Zicfilp
z_security.desc: Marks valid indirect-branch targets with landing pads, trapping calls and jumps that land anywhere else.

mseccfgh.desc: Most significant 32 bits of Machine Security Configuration

z_security.name: Zicfiss
z_security.desc: Keeps return addresses on a protected shadow stack and checks them on return, blocking stack-smashing ROP.

z_crypto.name: Zbkb
z_crypto.desc: Rotations, byte packing, and bit reversal used heavily inside cipher and hash implementations.
z_crypto.use: Rotations, pack and byte-reverse for crypto

z_crypto.name: Zbkc
z_crypto.desc: Carry-less multiplication over GF(2) polynomials, the core operation behind AES-GCM's GHASH.

z_crypto.name: Zbkx
z_crypto.desc: Crossbar permutations that build 4- and 8-bit lookup tables in registers for constant-time S-boxes.

z_crypto.name: Zk
z_crypto.desc: Shorthand bundle for the NIST scalar crypto suite, the entropy source CSR, and timing-safety guarantees.
z_crypto.use: Selecting the standard scalar crypto bundle

z_crypto.name: Zkn
z_crypto.desc: Shorthand for the NIST-algorithm scalar set: AES encryption and decryption, SHA-2, and crypto bitmanip.

z_crypto.name: Zknd
z_crypto.desc: Accelerates AES decryption rounds and the inverse key schedule in the general-purpose registers.

z_crypto.name: Zkne
z_crypto.desc: Accelerates AES encryption rounds and key expansion in the general-purpose registers.

z_crypto.name: Zknh
z_crypto.desc: Accelerates the round and message-schedule functions of SHA-256 and SHA-512 from the SHA-2 family.

z_crypto.name: Zkr
z_crypto.desc: Defines the seed CSR, which returns physical entropy for seeding cryptographic random bit generators.

mseccfgh.desc: Most significant 32 bits of Machine Security Configuration

z_crypto.name: Zks
z_crypto.desc: Shorthand for the Chinese ShangMi scalar set: the SM4 block cipher, the SM3 hash, and crypto bitmanip.

z_crypto.name: Zksed
z_crypto.desc: Accelerates the SM4 block cipher, whose single core operation serves both encryption and decryption.

z_crypto.name: Zksh
z_crypto.desc: Accelerates the SM3 cryptographic hash, the ShangMi counterpart to SHA-256.

z_crypto.name: Zkt
z_crypto.desc: Guarantees data-independent execution latency for a listed subset of instructions, closing timing leaks.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvbc32e
z_vector_crypto.desc: Carryless multiply on 32-bit vector elements, bringing GCM and CRC acceleration to ELEN=32 embedded cores.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvkb
z_vector_crypto.desc: Vector rotations, byte reversal, and and-not operations that underpin cipher and hash kernels.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvkg
z_vector_crypto.desc: Vector GHASH instructions for the Galois-field multiply behind AES-GCM and GMAC authentication.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvkgs
z_vector_crypto.desc: Vector-scalar forms of the GHASH instructions, letting one hash key drive many blocks of GCM at once.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvkn
z_vector_crypto.desc: Shorthand for the vector NIST suite: AES, SHA-2 up to SHA-512, crypto bitmanip, and timing safety.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvknc
z_vector_crypto.desc: Vector NIST algorithm suite bundled with carry-less multiply for Galois-field arithmetic.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvkned
z_vector_crypto.desc: Vector AES rounds and key schedule over 128-bit element groups, with data-independent timing.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvknf
z_vector_crypto.desc: Proposed full-round AES-128 and AES-256 encrypt, decrypt, and key-schedule vector instructions.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvkng
z_vector_crypto.desc: Vector NIST algorithm suite bundled with the GHASH instructions for complete AES-GCM coverage.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvknha
z_vector_crypto.desc: Vector acceleration of the SHA-256 rounds and message schedule, the 256-bit half of SHA-2.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvknhb
z_vector_crypto.desc: Vector SHA-2 acceleration covering both SHA-256 and SHA-512, unlike the SHA-256-only Zvknha.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvks
z_vector_crypto.desc: Shorthand for the vector ShangMi suite: SM4, SM3, crypto bitmanip, and data-independent timing.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvksc
z_vector_crypto.desc: Vector ShangMi algorithm suite bundled with carry-less multiply for Galois-field arithmetic.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvksed
z_vector_crypto.desc: Vector SM4 encryption, decryption, and key-schedule steps over 128-bit element groups.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvksg
z_vector_crypto.desc: Vector ShangMi algorithm suite bundled with the GHASH instructions for GCM authentication.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvksh
z_vector_crypto.desc: Vector SM3 acceleration covering message expansion and compression over 256-bit element groups.

z_vector_crypto.name: Zvkt
z_vector_crypto.desc: Guarantees that a listed set of vector instructions runs in time independent of data values, closing timing side channels.

z_system.name: Zibi
z_system.desc: Conditional branches that compare a register against a small constant, avoiding a separate load of that constant.
z_system.use: Loops and comparisons against small constants

z_system.name: Zicntr
z_system.desc: Unprivileged read access to the CYCLE, TIME and INSTRET counters for cycle count, real time and instructions retired.
z_system.use: Cycle and instruction counting for profiling

cycleh.desc: High-half cycle counter for RDCYCLE Instruction

instret.desc: Instructions retired counter for RDINSTRET Instruction

z_system.name: Zicsr
z_system.desc: Instructions to read, write and atomically modify control and status registers, the interface to most machine state.
z_system.use: Any code that reads or writes CSRs

z_system.name: Zifencei
z_system.desc: FENCE.I synchronizes a hart's writes to instruction memory with its own instruction fetches, as JITs and loaders require.

z_system.name: Zihintntl
z_system.desc: Hints marking the next memory access as having poor temporal locality, so caches need not retain the data.

z_system.name: Zihintpause
z_system.desc: PAUSE hints that the hart should slow instruction retirement, cutting energy waste in spin-wait loops.

z_system.name: Zihpm
z_system.desc: Up to 29 programmable event counters, hpmcounter3 through hpmcounter31, for profiling and performance tuning.

z_system.name: Zimop
z_system.desc: Reserves encodings that simply write zero today, letting later extensions redefine them without breaking old code.

z_system.name: Zimt
z_system.desc: Tags 16-byte memory chunks and checks the tag on each pointer dereference, catching use-after-free and overruns.

z_system.name: Zjid
z_system.desc: Draft J-extension mechanism for instruction and data synchronization, offered as an alternative to Zifencei's FENCE.I.
z_system.use: Alternative to Zifencei for I-cache coherence

z_system.name: Zjpm
z_system.desc: Pointer masking lets a hart ignore upper address bits so software can keep tags there, as HWASAN-style checkers do.

z_system.name: Ztso
z_system.desc: Stricter memory ordering in which every load and store carries implicit acquire or release semantics, as on x86.

z_caches.name: Zic64b
z_caches.desc: Asserts that cache blocks are exactly 64 bytes and naturally aligned, which cache-block instructions rely on.
z_caches.use: Software tuned to a 64-byte cache line

z_caches.name: Zicbom
z_caches.desc: Instructions to invalidate, clean or flush a cache block by address, for DMA and device-shared buffers.
z_caches.use: Keeping caches coherent with DMA and devices

z_caches.name: Zicbop
z_caches.desc: Software-directed prefetch of a cache block for reading, writing or instruction fetch, to hide memory latency.

z_caches.name: Zicboz
z_caches.desc: Zeroes a whole cache block in one instruction, speeding memset and bulk clearing of memory.

z_caches.name: Ziccamoa
z_caches.desc: Asserts that cacheable, coherent main memory supports every arithmetic atomic operation in the A extension.

z_caches.name: Ziccamoc
z_caches.desc: Asserts that cacheable, coherent main memory supports compare-and-swap atomics at the AMOCASQ level.

z_caches.name: Ziccid
z_caches.desc: Stricter consistency between instruction fetch and data accesses than the base ISA requires, easing run-time code patching.

z_caches.name: Ziccif
z_caches.desc: Asserts that cacheable, coherent main memory supports instruction fetch and that aligned fetches are atomic.

s_mem.name: Sv32
s_mem.desc: Two-level page tables map 32-bit virtual addresses to 34-bit physical addresses on RV32 systems.

s_mem.name: Sv39
s_mem.desc: Three-level page tables give RV64 harts a 39-bit virtual address space, the usual choice for Linux.
s_mem.use: Paged virtual memory with a 512 GB address space

s_mem.name: Sv48
s_mem.desc: Four-level page tables widen the RV64 virtual address space to 48 bits for larger memory footprints.
s_mem.use: Paged virtual memory with a 256 TB address space

s_mem.name: Sv57
s_mem.desc: Five-level page tables widen the RV64 virtual address space to 57 bits for very large memory footprints.
s_mem.use: Paged virtual memory with a 128 PB address space

s_mem.name: Svbare
s_mem.desc: Requires satp mode Bare, so supervisor software can run with address translation switched off.
s_mem.use: Systems that run without address translation
s_mem.behavior:
This extension mandates that the `satp` mode Bare must
be supported.

[NOTE]
This extension was ratified as part of the RVA22 profile.

s_mem.name: Svpbmt
s_mem.desc: Two PTE bits set a page's memory type as non-cacheable or I/O, overriding the region's default attributes.

s_mem.name: Svnapot
s_mem.desc: Marks a naturally aligned power-of-two run of pages as one translation, easing TLB pressure on large mappings.
s_mem.behavior:
In Sv39, Sv48, and Sv57, when a PTE has N=1, the PTE represents a
translation that is part of a range of contiguous virtual-to-physical
translations with the same values for PTE bits 5-0. Such ranges must be
of a naturally aligned power-of-2 (NAPOT) granularity larger than the
base page size.

s_mem.name: Svinval
s_mem.desc: Splits the SFENCE.VMA family into finer invalidate and ordering operations that pipeline better on wide cores.

s_mem.name: Svade
s_mem.desc: Hardware never updates the accessed and dirty bits in a PTE; it raises a page fault so software can set them.
s_mem.use: Hardware that traps rather than sets A/D bits
s_mem.behavior:
The Svade extension indicates that hardware does *not* update the A/D bits of a page table
during a page walk. Rather, encountering a PTE with the A bit clear or the D bit clear when
an operation is a write will cause a Page Fault.

s_mem.name: Svadu
s_mem.desc: Hardware sets the accessed and dirty bits in page table entries, sparing software a fault on every update.
s_mem.long_name: Hardware Updating of PTE A/D Bits

s_mem.name: Svvptc
s_mem.desc: Invalid-to-valid PTE updates become visible to the hart within bounded time, so no SFENCE.VMA is needed.
s_mem.long_name: Guarantee visibility of PTE transitions from invalid to valid
s_mem.behavior:
When the Svvptc extension is implemented, explicit stores by a hart that update
the Valid bit of leaf and/or non-leaf PTEs from 0 to 1 and are visible to a hart
will eventually become visible within a bounded timeframe to subsequent implicit
accesses by that hart to such PTEs.

If the Svrsw60t59b extension is implemented, then bits 60-59 of the page table
entries (PTEs) are reserved for use by supervisor software and are ignored by
the implementation.

s_mem.name: Svatag

with some facility provided in the application execution environment to control pointer masking.

s_mem.name: Ssnpm
s_mem.desc: Supervisor-level control of pointer masking for the next lower privilege mode, U-mode and the virtualized modes.
s_mem.long_name: Pointer masking for next privilege level less than S-mode
s_mem.behavior:
A supervisor-level extension that provides pointer masking for the next lower privilege mode (U-mode),
and for VS-modes and VU-modes if the H extension is present.

s_mem.name: Sspm
s_mem.desc: Asserts that pointer masking is available in supervisor mode, with its controls managed by the execution environment.
s_mem.long_name: Pointer masking available in supervisor mode
s_mem.behavior:

with some facility provided in the application execution environment to control pointer masking.

It is intended to be used

s_mem.name: Ssccptr
s_mem.desc: Requires cacheable and coherent main memory to support hardware page-table reads during a walk.
s_mem.use: Hardware page-table walks in cacheable memory
s_mem.long_name: Cacheable and coherent main memory page table reads
s_mem.behavior:
Main memory regions with both the cacheability and coherence PMAs must support hardware page-table reads.

[NOTE]
This extension was ratified with the RVA20 profiles.

s_mem.name: Smvatag
s_mem.desc: Holds M-mode memory-tagging tags in a virtually indexed table located by the new mvitt base register.

s_mem.name: Smepmp
s_mem.desc: Machine-mode access and execution prevention built on PMP, so firmware cannot reach untrusted memory by default.
s_mem.long_name: PMP Enhancements for memory access and execution prevention on Machine mode

s_mem.desc: Machine-level control of pointer masking for the next privilege level down, S/HS, or U when S is absent.
s_mem.long_name: Pointer masking for next privilege level less than M-mode
s_mem.behavior:
A machine-level extension that provides pointer masking for the next lower privilege mode
(S/HS if S-mode is implemented, or U-mode otherwise).

s_mem.desc: A memory-type field in each PMP entry overrides the physical memory attributes for accesses that match it.
s_mem.use: Overriding memory attributes per PMP region
s_mem.behavior:
The Smpmpmt extension provides a mechanism analogous to Svpbmt but associated
with the PMP registers rather than page-table entries.
A new WARL field, MT (Memory Type), is added in the unallocated bits 6--5 in
each PMP configuration register.

s_mem.name: Sspmp
s_mem.desc: Supervisor-mode physical memory protection: per-hart entries that grant or revoke read, write and execute on physical regions without paging.
s_mem.use: Task isolation on MCU-class cores that have no MMU

s_mem.name: Sspmpen
s_mem.desc: A bitmask CSR that activates SPMP entries individually, so a context switch is one register write instead of reprogramming up to 128 registers.
s_mem.use: Cutting SPMP context-switch cost on RTOS workloads
s_mem.long_name: Extension for Optimizing Context Switching of SPMP Entries

spmpenh.desc: Upper 32 bits of SPMP entry enable (RV32 only)

s_mem.name: Smpmpdeleg
s_mem.desc: Delegates a contiguous range of M-mode PMP entries to supervisor mode, where they become SPMP entries, so one block of hardware serves both.
s_mem.use: Reusing PMP hardware instead of duplicating it for SPMP
s_mem.long_name: Extension for Sharing Hardware Resources between PMP and SPMP

s_interrupt.name: Smaia
s_interrupt.desc: Machine-level half of the Advanced Interrupt Architecture, adding message-signaled interrupts and more causes.
s_interrupt.use: Scalable interrupt delivery at machine level

s_interrupt.name: Ssaia
s_interrupt.desc: Supervisor-level half of the Advanced Interrupt Architecture, exposing its CSRs and behavior below M-mode.

hstateen0h.desc: Upper 32 bits of Hypervisor State Enable 0 Register

mstateen0h.desc: Upper 32 bits of Machine State Enable 0 Register

s_interrupt.name: Smclic
s_interrupt.desc: Machine-mode core-local interrupt controller giving each interrupt its own level, priority and preemption.

s_interrupt.name: Smclicconfig
s_interrupt.desc: Makes the CLIC's split between interrupt level and priority bits programmable rather than fixed in hardware.

s_interrupt.name: Smclicshv
s_interrupt.desc: Lets each CLIC interrupt pick hardware vectoring for lower latency or software vectoring for smaller code.

s_interrupt.name: Ssclic
s_interrupt.desc: Extends the core-local interrupt controller to S-mode, so supervisor interrupts are taken without M-mode.

s_interrupt.name: Sstc
s_interrupt.desc: Lets S-mode and VS-mode set their own timer deadlines directly, avoiding a call down to machine-mode firmware.

s_interrupt.name: Sscofpmf
s_interrupt.desc: Fires a local interrupt when a performance counter overflows and filters counting by privilege mode.
s_interrupt.long_name: Counter Overflow and Privilege Mode Filtering

s_interrupt.name: Shlcofideleg
s_interrupt.desc: Makes hideleg bit 13 writable, so a hypervisor can delegate local counter overflow interrupts to VS-mode.
s_interrupt.use: Delegating counter overflow to a guest
s_interrupt.long_name: Hypervisor local counter overflow interrupt delegation
s_interrupt.behavior:
When implemented, bit 13 of `hideleg` is writable, which lets Local Counter Overflow Interrupts (LCOFIs) be delegated to VS-mode.

[NOTE]
Requires H and Sscofpmf: the interrupt it delegates is the one Sscofpmf defines, and the register it makes writable belongs to H.

s_interrupt.name: Ssqosid
s_interrupt.desc: Tags a hart's memory requests with workload IDs so shared caches and bandwidth can be allocated and monitored.

s_interrupt.name: Smrnmi
s_interrupt.desc: Saves the interrupted state in dedicated CSRs so a non-maskable interrupt handler can return with mnret.

s_interrupt.name: Smsdia
s_interrupt.desc: Assigns IMSIC interrupt files and APLIC domains to individual supervisor domains for isolated delivery.

s_counters.name: Smcdeleg
s_counters.desc: Lets M-mode delegate performance counters and event selectors to S-mode, avoiding traps into machine mode.

s_counters.name: Smcntrpmf
s_counters.desc: Stops the cycle and instret counters from counting in selected privilege modes, for cleaner measurements.
s_counters.long_name: Cycle and Instret Privilege Mode Filtering

s_counters.name: Ssccfg
s_counters.desc: Supervisor-mode CSRs for configuring and inhibiting the performance counters that M-mode has delegated.

s_counters.name: Sscounterenw
s_counters.desc: Every implemented hardware performance counter must have a writable enable bit in scounteren.
s_counters.long_name: Support writeable enables for any supported counter
s_counters.behavior:
For any hpmcounter that is not read-only zero, the corresponding bit in `scounteren` must be writable.

[NOTE]
This extension was ratified with the RVA22 profiles.

mstateen0h.desc: Upper 32 bits of Machine State Enable 0 Register

It also allows M-mode to invoke a critical error handler in the OS/Hypervisor on a double trap in S/HS-mode.

`stval` must be written with the faulting virtual address for load, store,
and instruction page-fault, access-fault, and misaligned exceptions,
and for breakpoint exceptions other than those caused by execution of the
`ebreak` or `c.ebreak instructions.

s_trap.name: Sstvecd
s_trap.desc: Guarantees stvec can be set to Direct mode, sending every supervisor trap to a single handler address.
s_trap.behavior:
`stvec.MODE` must be capable of holding the value 0 (Direct).
When `stvec.MODE`=Direct, `stvec.BASE` must be capable of holding any valid
four-byte-aligned address.

s_trap.name: Sstvecv
s_trap.desc: Guarantees stvec supports Vectored mode, so each interrupt cause can dispatch to its own entry point.
s_trap.behavior:
`stvec.MODE` must be capable of holding the value 1 (Vectored).
When `stvec.MODE`=Vectored, interrupts set `pc` to `stvec.BASE + 4 * cause`,
allowing each interrupt source to have its own entry point.
Synchronous exceptions still use the base address regardless of the mode.

s_trap.name: Ssdtso
s_trap.desc: Lets supervisor software switch a hart between the RVWMO and TSO memory models at run time, per process.

s_trap.name: Sstcfg
s_trap.desc: Supervisor-side half of trigger delegation, giving S-mode and VS-mode debuggers direct access to Sdtrig triggers.

s_trap.name: Ssstrict
s_trap.desc: Guarantees that reserved standard encodings raise illegal-instruction traps and no non-conforming extensions exist.
s_trap.long_name: Unimplemented reserved encodings trap and no non-conforming extensions
s_trap.behavior:
No non-conforming extensions are present.  Attempts to
execute unimplemented opcodes or access unimplemented CSRs in the
standard or reserved encoding spaces raises an illegal instruction
exception that results in a contained trap to the supervisor-mode
trap handler.

s_trap.name: Ssu32xl
s_trap.desc: Lets U-mode run 32-bit code on a 64-bit machine by allowing sstatus.UXL to select UXLEN=32.
s_trap.behavior:
`sstatus.UXL` must be capable of holding the value 1 (i.e., UXLEN=32 must be supported).

This allows U-mode to run 32-bit code on a 64-bit machine by setting `sstatus.UXL` to 1.

s_trap.name: Ssu64xl
s_trap.desc: Requires 64-bit user mode to be supported, so sstatus.UXL can select UXLEN=64.
s_trap.behavior:
`sstatus.UXL` must be capable of holding the value 2 (i.e., UXLEN=64 must be supported).

[NOTE]
This extension is defined by RVA22.

s_trap.name: Ssube
s_trap.desc: Lets U-mode data accesses use big-endian byte order while instruction fetch stays little-endian.
s_trap.behavior:
`sstatus.UBE` must be capable of holding the value 1 (i.e., big-endian user mode must be supported).

When `sstatus.UBE` is set to 1, data accesses in U-mode use big-endian byte ordering.
Instructions are always fetched as little-endian regardless of this setting.

s_trap.name: Smtdeleg
s_trap.desc: Delegates Sdtrig debug triggers to S-mode and VS-mode through indirect CSRs, avoiding traps into M-mode.

s_trap.name: RERI

s_trap.name: HTI
s_trap.desc: Standard interface between a RISC-V hart and a trace encoder, defining how the hart supplies instruction trace information.

** *H* The hypervisor extension.

** *Ssstateen* Supervisor-mode view of the state-enable extension.  The

s_trap.name: Shcounterenw
s_trap.desc: Every implemented hpmcounter must have a writable hcounteren bit, so a hypervisor can delegate counters to guests.
s_trap.use: Guests that need writable counter enables
s_trap.behavior:
For any hpmcounter that is not read-only zero, the corresponding bit in `hcounteren` must be writable.

[NOTE]
This extension was ratified with the RVA22 profiles.

s_trap.name: Shgatpa

s_trap.desc: Guest-physical translation must offer an SvNNx4 mode for every satp mode supported, plus Bare.

s_trap.behavior:
For each supported virtual memory scheme SvNN supported in
`satp`, the corresponding hgatp SvNNx4 mode must be supported.  The
`hgatp` mode Bare must also be supported.

[NOTE]
This extension was ratified with the RVA22 profiles.

s_trap.desc: htval must record the faulting guest-physical address wherever the ISA allows, sparing the hypervisor from decoding it.
s_trap.long_name: Hypervisor Trap Value provides all needed values
s_trap.behavior:
htval must be written with the faulting guest physical address in all circumstances permitted by
the ISA.

[NOTE]
This extension was ratified with the RVA22 profiles.

s_trap.name: Shvsatpa
s_trap.short: Virtual Supervisor address translation supports all supported S-mode modes
s_trap.desc: vsatp must support every translation mode that satp supports, so a guest OS sees the same paging choices.

s_trap.behavior:
All translation modes supported in the `satp` CSR must be supported in the `vsatp` CSR.

[NOTE]
This extension was ratified with the RVA22 profiles.

for load, store, and instruction page-fault, access-fault, and

those caused by execution of the `ebreak` or `c.ebreak` instructions.
